correctness.rationale: For the ordinary (not total) five-cut complex of the nine-vertex 3×3 grid, independently enumerate all C(9,5)=126 five-subsets and test induced connectivity; 77 disconnected subsets yield 77 complementary four-vertex facets. Closure yields 202 nonempty faces and f=(9,36,80,77). The staged row-major-toggle matching has 88 pairs and an acyclic orientation verified over 620 Hasse covers; exactly one critical vertex and 25 critical three-cells remain, no positive cells in dimensions one or two. Forman theory therefore gives an actual wedge of 25 S³, stronger than homology rank. The prior literature's 25 is an existing Betti table entry, not an independent proof of this homotopy type.

evidence: Bayer et al prove grid wedge for k=3,4; for k=5 they analyze faces and Euler characteristic, with Table 2 computing β=25 for 3×3. Chandrakar et al treat other grid widths or total cut, so do not cover ordinary k=5 square grid.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No known broad result inspected implies pure 25 copies of S³ here; rational Betti 25 alone is insufficient.

A complete finite Morse collapse from a known Betti number to an integral homotopy decomposition is substantive because matching Betti ranks do not determine homotopy type or torsion/attaching structure in general. It is a benchmark, not an all-grid classification.
